summary: The input already parses Detransitive senses 2–5. Many reader claims that it only contains forms, or that D1 is a printed motion sense, are stale summaries. Preserve the supplied numbering, including the inherited čīk/mičək within the sense-2 gloss.

Active insertion has an L-series agent and an object; self-motion can use active ruḥo or Detransitive čīk/mičək without ruḥo. Farida /27 places these constructions side by side. Detransitive institutional entry may imply external placement, but no agent is expressed.

The lebo-subject construction in sense 4 encodes the experiencer as heart possessor and the stimulus with b-. The English in Fingan /30 reverses that image, and must not determine Turoyo argument analysis.

Infectum-wa has habitual retreat and prevention, and a counterfactual. Detransitive Preterit can set a future temporal boundary (Xalaf /75); ko-Preterit has current result. No one-to-one tense meaning is inferred.

Routine counts are aggregate supplementary evidence, not additional occurrence decisions. Their D1/D2 split is a reader indexing inconsistency, not evidence for a new D1 sense; do not sum them as distinct meanings.
The inherited baxt appeals, including the fathers’ graves passage, are already idioms. Their performative Preterit/Infectum distribution remains open. No duplicate idiom is added.

Lookup searches in inputs/glossary_lookup.py for qərrəq (no hits), šamṯo, and baxt preceded the collocation decision. Kurdish derivation is inherited; these contexts alone cannot date or prove a contact-induced construction.

Batch 2 continues all batch-1 changes, numbers, corrections and selected examples. Current occurrence decisions concern only the 126 supplied batch-2 occurrences; prior decisions remain in batch 1. No earlier decision was overturned.

Conversation b-ǧġaliye recurs across 65/157, 65/159, 66/86 and is treated as one idiom. Throat/neck reciprocal confrontation in 65/518 and 66/10 corroborates the batch-1 collocation, including actual blows in 65/518.

The Detransitive emotional frames differ: ʕal lebo with grief (2b), lebo subject with b-stimulus (4), and ḥubo subject with reciprocal bayn (participant/coding extension of 4). These are established from the Turoyo, not subject choices in the German.

The existing 78/113 Detransitive Infectum example begins with Preterit čik and includes Infectum mičək in the wolf simile. Retain the whole mixed-form example; its presence is not a reason to reclassify the first token as Infectum.
Permitted glossary searches: ǧġaliye, ḥṭiṯ, gež, qḏole. Existing idioms under other verbs were distinguished from the new čyk combinations.
The batch-1 ko-Preterit correction already handles the exact 65/466 example. Talay 1/280 and /282 already occur within the inherited combined LB passage; no duplicate text added.

Every reader D1 motion label is resolved to the entry's existing Detransitive 2. Round 1 already explains this stale indexing problem and supplies Detransitive Preterit-wa and active Infectum-wa; none is newly claimed here.

Active insertion has an agent L-ending and a moved object, while Detransitive čik/mičək takes the entering participant as subject. Government as entering subject in war belongs to D2, not D3 where ḥarb itself breaks out.
Debt uses taḥt as an abstract destination; mnasaba arises bayn people. Record each collocation once. Relationship formation does not itself establish affection or consent.
Literary institutional destinations in the Jan interviews coexist with colloquial contracted forms. No register change by itself establishes a new lexical sense.
Confirm whether čikono in LuF 3/30 and čəkno in baxt appeals are Detransitive Preterit forms or dialectal active Infectum; both spellings occur in inherited idioms.
Does čīḳwa in ṣaḥwo čīḳwa (Farida /49) belong to čyk, and what exactly does the phrase mean?
In NE Famine /67 do the thorns protrude from the vessel or still prick/penetrate hands? The English alone does not establish outward direction.
Is the throat collocation in Numan /66 literal physical choking, figurative quarrelling, or both?

Resolve the boy/girl object mismatch in JTM 1.6/3, the unrendered čyk clauses in PrS 58/112, 71/43, 74/110, 75/78 and 80/69, and the missing independent English clause in Hanna Dewo /136 before quoting them.
Confirm active Infectum versus Detransitive Preterit čiki in Unfortunate Youth /25; the objectless narrative favors the latter.
Verify the nominal senses of mŭkus (Xalaf /63), be ʕəbraṯe (29/485), and kawno (Aḥmad /59); do not infer gaze, degradation, or glory from translation alone.
The LB 280–282 example combines plain and ko-prefixed Detransitive Preterit tokens. Should it be split into dedicated boxes with its original source available?
The existing PrS page references and numbered input verse references are different systems. Confirm correspondence before changing citations; no guessed conversion is proposed.
66/56 has a translation mismatch explicitly reported by the reader: recover its own edition translation before adding nuro čik b-hnavo; no translation from adjacent /57 was silently imported.
Verify čikənne at 65/157 and 66/86 against ordinary plural čiki; do not infer a separate stem.
Confirm whether the head/heart lexemes in 66/68–69 and 89/67 support the proposed construction labels, and whether qḏole and qərrəqe are interchangeable in the hostile reciprocal idiom.
At 69/148 the Turoyo qum šeno and German hinter einen Felsen differ spatially; at 65/546 the day/time endpoints remain unclear.
Confirm ṭomke (95/219), čʕəkle (105/99), and the subject of the final clause in 104/40 from the source or speakers; no normalized wording supplied.
Does čiko in 75/138 itself encode mechanical wedging, or does the closing-door context alone supply it? Current analysis merges it into 2.
The active Infectum čiki b-qamayto at Talay 1/290 is an existing filing; verify its relation to Detransitive Preterit čīk and refrain from inferring a new form from spelling alone.
Confirm first-person čəkno at Jan 1.8/180 as Detransitive Preterit in the reported entry event rather than active Infectum with an omitted object.

Does bayn- in the mediation contexts lexicalize intervention beyond ordinary entering between? It is provisionally kept under D2 because the inherited lion-interposition example already has this configuration.

Ein Mensch als zizono wird von Gott zwischen andere gesetzt; im entsprechenden Detransitive drängt er sich als Störenfried hinein.
The coercive legal-affair b-daʕwa construction confirms round-1 figurative involvement in difficulties; do not propose it again.

Detransitive bayn-participants supports physical interposition and mediation; intervention by a sheikh, priest, authorities and relatives extends the existing entering-between construction rather than establishing a separate sense.
Detransitive entry covers school classes and institutional membership, alongside houses, gaps, mouth penetration, and prison. No extra numbered senses are needed for the kind of destination.
